title: The Hilbert space of n qubits
caption: Joining systems multiplies dimensions: n qubits live in a 2ⁿ-dimensional space. 3 qubits need 8 amplitudes (the lesson's example), 10 qubits 1,024, 20 qubits about 10⁶ and 50 qubits 2⁵⁰ ≈ 10¹⁵: 14 orders of magnitude more than 3 qubits, which is why simulating them classically is hard.
alt: A logarithmic scale of Hilbert-space dimension from 1 to 10^16 with 3 qubits at 8, 10 qubits at 1024, 20 qubits at about a million and 50 qubits at about 10^15.
description: A horizontal logarithmic scale of the number of amplitudes (the dimension of the Hilbert space).
Each added qubit doubles the dimension, so the numbers grow exponentially.

claims.name: 50 qubits have 2^47 times the dimension of 3 qubits
